parsed.paper: The Resurrection Connection to Christian Theology - Gary Habermas with @Real Seekers

core_relation.sentence: The resurrection is the linchpin that, if granted, entails a God who raised Jesus, the deity of Christ, the kingdom of God, and the truth of his teaching; all other doctrines hang on this one event.
core_relation.quote: Now, if you put it together, this event happened. That requires this being. [S230-S232]

product_test.quote: If there's a resurrection, somebody had to do it... If Jesus is raised from the dead and his leading teaching is true. [S256, S262]
product_test.reason: Habermas treats the resurrection as a necessary condition: if it did not occur, the entire theological edifice (God, deity of Christ, kingdom, salvation) collapses. The relation is stated as conditional entailment, not additive weakening.

slots.plays_role: External negentropy influx is the resurrection itself as an act of God breaking into history from outside; coherence of doctrine cannot sustain itself without this external event.
slots.quote: If God raised Jesus, if there's a resurrection and there's a God, you got to link the two. [S236]

slots.plays_role: Alignment is the correspondence between Jesus's claims/teaching and the resurrection event; the resurrection is the divine alignment with Jesus's own predictions.
slots.quote: If Jesus is raised from the dead and his leading teaching is true. [S262]

slots.plays_role: Signal fidelity is the historical evidence and eyewitness testimony for the resurrection that survives skeptical noise; Habermas insists on evidential transmission.
slots.quote: It's always empirical evidence like near-death experiences, uh Shroud of Turin, or historical evidence for the resurrection. [S108]

slots.plays_role: Effective entropy is the skepticism, doubt, and competing miracle claims that lower coherence; Habermas treats these as noise to be answered, not as a factor that can be zeroed out.
slots.quote: If they're really skeptical, no matter what I say will make no difference. [S084]

slots.plays_role: Temporal integration is the 15-year project and the cumulative historical case built across four volumes; time turns the possibility of resurrection into accumulated evidence.
slots.quote: Obviously, this is a project that took you 15 years. [S023]

slots.plays_role: Compression is the compression of the entire theological system into two key words: theology and practice; the four volumes compress ordered meaning.
slots.quote: The two key words in the title, what the resurrection means for theology and what the resurrection means um in practice. [S041]

slots.plays_role: Phase transition is the resurrection as a one-time, unique event that changes state, not degree; it is a threshold that authenticates a religion.
slots.quote: It's a one-time event where the evidence is very good. It occurred and it is for the purpose of evidencing a message. [S440-S441]

slots.plays_role: Superposition is the open possibility of the resurrection before evidence is assessed; it remains unresolved until actualized by historical investigation.
slots.quote: If something like that happened, yeah, it would be it would be the biggie. [S458]

slots.plays_role: Non-local correlation is the connection between the resurrection and other doctrines (deity, kingdom, scripture) that are no longer independent once the event is granted.
slots.quote: I think scriptures entailed somewhere down the line, just like I think ethics are entailed somewhere down the line. [S334]

slots.plays_role: Integration is Habermas himself as the integrator, synthesizing evidence, theology, and practice into a unified case across 52 books.
slots.quote: I've done 52 books and and by the way, I wouldn't know that except that I get asked once in a while. [S027]

breaks: The paper treats the resurrection as a singular, unrepeatable event; the master equation is a general integral over all events, not a one-time threshold.
Habermas explicitly denies that the relation is additive or probabilistic in the master-equation sense; he insists on a binary entailment (if resurrection, then God).
The slot Q (superposition) is largely absent: Habermas does not treat the resurrection as an unresolved possibility but as a historical fact to be proven.
The paper adds factors with no clear slot: the role of the Holy Spirit, the authority of scripture, and the personal commitment of the integrator (Habermas's own 52-year career).
extra_factors: The Holy Spirit as an additional agent in verification and understanding.
The authority of scripture as a self-authenticating source.
The personal faith and commitment of the researcher as a condition for seeing the evidence.
parsed.one_line: The resurrection functions as the external negentropy influx (G) whose occurrence multiplicatively entails the entire theological system, but the analogy is limited by the paper's binary, one-time, non-integral framing.
